q: Which Gulf country's maroon flag has a white serrated edge with nine points?
x: The maroon is said to come from a traditional dye that darkens in the heat of the sun.

q: Which Gulf kingdom's red flag has a white serrated band at the hoist with five points?
x: The five points are said to stand for the five pillars of Islam.

q: Which Central Asian country's flag has blue, white and green bands, a crescent and 12 stars?
x: Thin red lines separate the three main bands.

q: Which Central Asian country's red, white and green flag has a golden crown with seven stars?
x: The white stripe is wider than the red and green stripes.

q: Which Pacific country's red and green flag has a sideways yellow Y and a boar's tusk emblem?
x: The curled boar's tusk and crossed namele leaves are prized symbols of traditional culture.

q: Which country's blue and green flag has a yellow diagonal stripe and five white stars?
x: The five stars originally stood for the country's five main districts.

q: Which Pacific country's flag has orange and white diagonal bands and a white star with 24 points?
x: The 24 points stand for the 24 municipalities, and the two diagonal bands suggest the sunrise.

q: Which South American country's flag shows a different emblem on each side?
x: The front shows the national arms with the May Star, and the back shows the Treasury seal with a lion.

q: Which South American country's flag has nine blue and white stripes and a sun in the top left?
x: The sun is the Sun of May, and nine stripes stand for the original departments.

q: Which Central American country's flag has two men holding tools within a ring of leaves?
x: It is one of the few national flags to show human figures.

q: Which country's blue, yellow and red flag has an eagle holding a cross and an aurochs' head in the center?
x: The aurochs' head is an ancient symbol of the region's heritage.

q: Which kingdom surrounded by South Africa has a flag with a black traditional hat?
x: The hat, called the mokorotlo, is a traditional Basotho design.

q: Which Central African country's flag is divided diagonally into green, yellow and red?
x: The yellow diagonal band separates the green triangle at the top from the red one at the bottom.

q: Which West African country's flag has five green and yellow stripes, a red canton and a white star?
x: The white star sits in the red canton at the hoist.

q: Which Arab country has a plain horizontal tricolor of red, white and black with no emblem?
x: It uses the Pan-Arab colors without any emblem or star.

q: Which tiny Alpine principality added a golden crown to its blue and red flag after a clash at the 1936 Olympics?
x: Officials noticed that its flag was identical to Haiti's, so a crown was added in 1937.

q: In which year did the Union Flag gain St Patrick's red saltire?
x: The flag took its present form when Ireland joined Great Britain in the United Kingdom.

q: In which year was the Hinomaru officially made Japan's national flag by law?
x: The red-disc design had been used for centuries before it was given legal status.

q: In what year did Israel formally adopt its flag?
x: The design had been used by the Zionist movement since the late 1800s.

q: In which year was India's tricolor adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
x: It was adopted a few weeks before independence on August 15.

q: Which heraldist designed South Africa's flag, introduced on April 27, 1994?
x: Brownell was the state herald, and the flag was meant as a temporary design that stayed in use.

q: On Brazil's flag, the stars depict the sky over which city on the day the republic was proclaimed?
x: The date was November 15, 1889, and each star stands for a state.

q: Which Indian Ocean country's flag has four stripes, a green triangle, a white crescent and four stars?
x: The four stars and four stripes stand for the four main islands.

q: Which Gulf sultanate's flag has an emblem of crossed swords over a dagger?
x: The flag has white, red and green bands and a vertical red band at the hoist.

q: Which country's flag has bo leaves in the corners of a maroon panel?
x: The bo tree is sacred to Buddhists, who form the majority of the population.

q: Bhutan's flag is divided diagonally into which two colors?
x: Yellow stands for the king's secular authority, and orange for Buddhist spiritual tradition.

q: On Singapore's flag, the five stars stand for democracy, peace, progress, justice and what?
x: The stars are arranged in a circle beside a white crescent that symbolizes a young nation on the rise.

q: On Pakistan's flag, the crescent stands for progress, and the star stands for what?
x: The crescent and star sit in the middle of the green field.

q: Which general designed Argentina's flag in 1812?
x: Belgrano raised it for the first time on the banks of the Parana River.

q: Which Venezuelan revolutionary designed the ancestor of the yellow, blue and red flags of Gran Colombia?
x: Miranda flew his tricolor in 1806 during an expedition to free Venezuela.

q: Which Irish nationalist presented the green, white and orange tricolor in 1848?
x: He had seen the French tricolor on a visit to France and wanted a flag to unite the island.

q: At which Olympic Games was the five-ring Olympic flag first flown?
x: The flag was designed in 1913, but the First World War delayed its first appearance.

q: Which organization first adopted the circle of twelve gold stars on blue in 1955?
x: The European Communities took up the same flag in 1985.

q: Which country is notable for having a national flag with none of red, white or blue?
x: It uses only gold, green and black.

q: Nepal's crimson flag is bordered in which color?
x: The two pennants carry a white moon and a white sun.

q: What does 'Y Ddraig Goch,' the Welsh name for the Welsh flag, mean?
x: The red dragon has been linked to Wales for well over a thousand years.

q: Which Indian Ocean island nation's flag has five oblique bands in blue, yellow, red, white and green?
x: The bands fan out from the lower hoist corner.

q: Which island nation's blue flag has a circle of ten yellow stars?
x: The ten stars stand for the main islands of the archipelago.

q: Which island country's flag has a red triangle with two black stars and green and yellow stripes?
x: The two stars stand for the two main islands.

q: Which country's flag has a black diagonal band with two white stars between green and red triangles?
x: The two stars stand for the two islands that make up the nation.

q: Which West African country's flag has a red vertical band with a black star beside yellow and green bands?
x: The black star is a symbol of African unity, as on Ghana's flag.

q: Which northeast African country's flag has red, white and black bands with a green triangle at the hoist?
x: The red, white, black and green are all Pan-Arab colors.

q: In vexillology, what is a 'fimbriation'?
a: A thin border separating two colors
x: A white fimbriation edges the blue cross on Norway's flag.

q: The word vexillology comes from which Latin word?
x: A vexillum was a Roman military banner hung from a crossbar.

q: A flag with a V-shaped notch cut into the fly is described by which term?
x: Ceremonial flags and naval signals often use this shape.

q: The wheel on India's flag is taken from a lion capital found at which site?
x: The capital dates from the era of the emperor Ashoka.

q: The eagle on Mexico's flag recalls the legend of the founding of which Aztec city?
x: Tenochtitlan stood where Mexico City is today.

q: What does the Greek flag's nickname 'Galanolefki' mean?
x: Another name, Kyanolefko, has the same meaning.

q: Which weapons are crossed behind the Maasai shield on Kenya's flag?
x: The white lines around the stripes are called fimbriations.

q: Which country's flag is, by tradition, never flown at half-mast because it bears the Islamic creed?
x: The Shahada text on the flag is considered too sacred to be lowered.

q: What do the olive branches on Cyprus' flag symbolize?
x: The branches are meant to show harmony between the island's communities.

q: Which Pacific country's light blue flag has a Union Jack and nine yellow stars?
x: The stars are arranged like the layout of the nine islands.

q: How many green stars ring the parrot on Dominica's flag?
x: The stars stand for the ten parishes of the island.

q: How many stars appear on Grenada's flag?
x: Six are in the border, and one is on the central red disc.

q: What motto is written on the ribbon beneath the arms on Haiti's flag?
x: The French original is 'L'Union fait la force.'

q: Which Andean volcano appears on the coat of arms on Ecuador's flag?
x: Chimborazo is Ecuador's highest mountain.

q: Mount Triglav on Slovenia's flag belongs to which mountain range?
x: Triglav is the highest peak in Slovenia and is a national symbol.

q: How many times is 'Allahu Akbar' written along the edges of the bands on Iran's flag?
x: It appears 11 times on the green band and 11 times on the red band.

q: Which Arab kingdom's flag has a red triangle containing a white seven-pointed star?
x: The star's seven points stand for the first seven verses of the Quran's opening chapter.

q: The three stars on the Philippine flag stand for Luzon, the Visayas and which island group?
x: The white triangle also holds a sun with eight rays.

q: Which Central American country's flag has five stripes and a coat of arms on a white circle to the left?
x: The wide red center band is flanked by white and blue stripes.

q: Which West African country has vertical bands of red, yellow and green with no emblem, red at the hoist?
x: It is the mirror image of Mali's flag.

q: Which East African country's flag has a sky blue top half and a golden sun in the upper fly?
x: The sun has 24 rays.

q: Which East African country's flag has black, red and green stripes with a blue triangle and a gold star?
x: White fimbriations separate the three stripes.

q: In flag design, what is a 'charge'?
a: A symbol placed on the field
x: The maple leaf on Canada's flag is a charge.

q: What name is given to the national flag flown by a ship?
x: The Red Ensign and White Ensign are famous British examples.

q: A small flag flown from the bow of a ship is called a what?
x: The 'Union Jack' is thought by many to take its name from this use.

q: Which Danish king's army was said to see the Dannebrog fall from the sky?
x: The legend is set at the Battle of Lindanise in Estonia in 1219.

q: Which Scottish village is linked to the legend of a white cross appearing in the sky that inspired the saltire?
x: The village in East Lothian calls itself the birthplace of the Scottish flag.

q: How many horizontal rows of stars are on the 50-star US flag?
x: The rows alternate between six stars and five stars.

q: Who is generally credited with designing India's national flag in its original form?
x: Venkayya was an Indian freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh.

q: How many blue stripes does the flag of Cuba have?
x: Three blue and two white stripes alternate, with the red triangle at the hoist.

q: How many blue stripes does the flag of Greece have?
x: Five blue and four white stripes make up the nine bands.

q: What is the Malaysian flag called in Malay, a name that means 'Stripes of Glory'?
x: The name was chosen for the flag in 1997.

q: In which Italian city was the tricolor first adopted as a flag in 1797?
x: Italy celebrates Tricolore Day on January 7 each year.

q: Whose volunteer corps wore black, red and gold in 1813, helping inspire Germany's flag colors?
x: Its uniforms were black with red trim and gold buttons.

q: In which year did France formally adopt its vertical blue, white and red tricolor?
x: The National Convention set the vertical order of the colors in February 1794.

q: A legend about Austria's red-white-red colors is set during the siege of which city?
x: It tells of Duke Leopold V, whose white tunic was stained with blood except under his belt.

q: In which year did Iceland adopt its flag as the banner of an independent republic?
x: The republic was founded on June 17, 1944.

q: Which state's admission in 1959 first brought the US flag to 49 stars?
x: The 49-star flag lasted only one year, until Hawaii joined.

q: Which king ordered the first Union Flag, joining the English and Scottish crosses, in 1606?
x: He was already James VI of Scotland, and his crowns were joined in 1603.

q: The map on the United Nations emblem is centered on which point?
x: The map is framed by olive branches and shows all inhabited continents.

q: What is a flag with two equal horizontal bands of different colors called?
x: Poland's, Ukraine's and Indonesia's flags are bicolors.

q: Which American coined the word 'vexillology' in 1957?
x: Smith also helped found the first international society for flag studies.

q: Which Central African country's flag has a blue triangle at the hoist and a tree on its arms?
x: The tree is a silk-cotton tree, and the horizontal bands are green, white and red.

q: Which East African country's flag has a white saltire and three red stars in a white disc?
x: The saltire divides the flag into red and green triangles.

q: Which Central African country's sky blue flag has a red diagonal stripe edged in yellow and a yellow star?
x: The star sits in the upper hoist corner.

q: Which West African country's flag has a blue band edged in white between red and green bands?
x: The blue stands for the river that runs through the country.

q: Which animal holds a cocoa pod on the shield of Fiji's flag?
x: The shield also shows sugar cane and a coconut palm.

q: The Southern Cross on Papua New Guinea's flag is made up of how many stars?
x: They are the stars of the Southern Cross, set on the black half.

q: Which Caribbean country's blue flag has a gold triangle edged in white, with black and white triangles?
x: The triangles represent the island's volcanic peaks.

q: The 1917 tricolor of which country replaced an older red flag bearing a white elephant?
x: The country was then known as Siam, and the new flag was introduced by King Vajiravudh.

q: After the monarchy fell in 1910, Portugal's flag changed from blue and white to which two main colors?
x: The republic chose the colors of the revolutionaries.

q: What book lies open at the center of the Dominican Republic's flag?
x: It is one of the few national flags to show a book of scripture.

q: Angkor Wat, shown on Cambodia's flag, was built by which empire?
x: It was built in the early 1100s as a Hindu temple.

q: In which year was China's five-star red flag adopted?
x: It was chosen at the founding of the People's Republic, in the fall of 1949.

q: How many rays does the Sun of May have on Argentina's flag?
x: The rays alternate between straight and wavy.

q: Honduras shows a cluster of blue stars on its white band; how many are there?
x: They stand for the five states of the old Federal Republic of Central America.

q: Samoa's blue canton holds a constellation of how many white stars?
x: They form the Southern Cross on a blue canton.

q: How many horizontal stripes does Uganda's flag have?
x: The pattern is black, yellow and red, repeated twice.
